annotations.annotation_text: The iconic squawk of the seagulls (the Four Old Men) mocking King Mark, famously inspiring the naming of the subatomic particle by Murray Gell-Mann.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: The cuckolded older figure, representing HCE in his displaced, impotent state as he watches the younger generation usurp his place.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: The young, virile lover, a manifestation of Shaun/Shem, who takes Isolde away from the fading paternal authority.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: The young, desirable woman, an avatar of Issy, embodying the renewing force of love that leaves the old world behind.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: The spatial and emotional distancing of the lovers from King Mark, representing the inevitable progression of generational cycles.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: The reincarnated Four Old Men (Mamalujo) who act as a voyeuristic chorus, offering a cynical, squawking commentary on the romance.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: A structural nod to Richard Wagner's Tristan und Isolde, whose unresolved chromaticism Joyce weaves into the restless prose rhythm.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: Explicit connection to the operatic tradition, demonstrating how Joyce layered myth, music, and local Dublin lore into a single narrative thread.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org
